notes: Catalog of every command pattern the `nspe` CLI (utils/nspe_cli.py) dispatches to, built from two sources: (1) the working examples in testnspe.sh/nfl.sh/testpost.sh, each already paired with a plain-English description, and (2) a direct read of nspe_cli.py's dispatch branches, its embedded '_..._FORMAT_CATALOG' usage strings, and the 'Command syntax:' docstrings in the engines/ modules they call. To keep this current: when adding a new dispatch branch to nspe_cli.py, add a matching family here (and update its FORMAT_CATALOG string too, if one exists) rather than letting the two drift apart. Bracket notation `{...}` marks optional tokens; `<...>` marks a required placeholder; `|` separates alternatives. Every 'examples' entry was read from a verified-working source or spot-checked live via `python3 utils/nspe_cli.py ...` during construction of this file (noted where a check surfaced a gotcha).

families.name: compute
families.description: Sums a stat across a window of games (or filters to a min/max total) for one or more hitters; omit the player to scan the whole league.
families.notes: Also supports position-code prefixes (e.g. `nspe mlb c -hr min5 -season` filters to catchers) via engines/mlb/loader.py's POSITION_MAP -- undocumented in the shell scripts, found only by reading the loader.

families.name: trend
families.description: Players who hit a per-game threshold in at least A of their last B games.

families.name: yesterday trend
families.description: Players who hit the threshold in their exact calendar-yesterday game (not just 'most recent game', which could be from days ago if they didn't play yesterday).

families.name: stat-token + date window
families.description: Bare stat-token followed by a specific date or an N-day window runs a one-off stat scan; no -leaderboard needed.

families.name: streak
families.description: Every maximal run of N+ consecutive qualifying games, current season by default (or a given year/year-range).
families.notes: -streakN cannot be combined with -leaderboard or -lastA/B -- it is a separate engine (verified: `nspe mlb -leaderboard -streak3` errors).

families.name: splits (season/game breakdown)
families.description: Breaks a total down instead of collapsing it to one number: a single resolved season splits by game (each qualifying game listed with its date), a multi-season scope (explicit year range, -career, or no window at all) splits by season (each qualifying season listed with its total).
families.notes: Shared generic compute-engine feature also available for NBA/NHL (not CFB, and not NFL's own -splits -- see NFL family).

families.name: weighted heat-score leaderboard
families.description: Top-20 hitters by a weighted heat-score composite across all tracked stats (current season). Writes data/output/mlb_leaderboard.json.

families.name: per-stat count leaderboard
families.description: Ranks players by how many qualifying games they've had for one stat threshold; token order is interchangeable (-<stat>N -leaderboard also works).

families.name: postseason
families.description: Same compute/trend/streak grammar as the regular-season family, scoped to postseason gamelogs (mlbpost_run). Defaults to the current/most-recent postseason year unless a YYYY or YYYY-YYYY is supplied.

families.name: pitcher h2h / VFP
families.description: A starting pitcher's per-start summary vs one team; -vfp adds average first-pitch velocity.
examples: nspe mlb pitch Paul Skenes vs LAD -2026
nspe mlb pitch Paul Skenes vs LAD -2026 -vfp

families.name: pitcher leaderboard
families.description: Pitchers ranked by count of starts meeting a stat threshold (K, BB, HR allowed, etc).

families.name: team overview (-ov)
families.description: Aggregates a team's pitcher play-by-play by game: 3/6/9-down rates, K/BB totals, schedule completeness. Requires both -ov and -season.

families.name: team batting (bat)
families.description: Inverts the pitcher PBP corpus into a team-batting view: K/BB/HR/H rates, out-type breakdown, or per-game hits/total-bases.

families.name: team batting vs pitcher
families.description: A team's collective batting line against one specific opposing pitcher.
examples: nspe mlb bat braves vs wheeler
families.notes: Spot-checked live; works and returns K/BB/HR/H/HBP breakdown.

families.name: team report (-teamreport)
families.description: Single-team hits/runs for-and-allowed plus average margin of victory/loss, sourced from the daily scoreboard scrape. Distinct from -ov (pitching-mechanics focus, different data source).
families.notes: Not present in any of the three shell scripts -- found only via engine docstring, spot-checked live.

families.name: team runs/hits (league-wide)
families.description: Scans/ranks all 30 teams by runs scored or allowed (2026-season-only data source); every result also carries the companion hits total for the same window.
families.notes: `nspe mlb team -runs` alone (no min/max/-leaderboard/-lastA-B) errors with a format catalog, by design.

families.name: team margin/spread scan
families.description: Scans teams by per-game score margin (win or loss size); -exactN and min/max are mutually exclusive; no -leaderboard or -lastA/B support for this sub-family.
families.notes: Not in any shell script -- found only via the _MLB_TEAM_FORMAT_CATALOG usage string; spot-checked live.

families.name: player report card
families.description: Weighted A++ through E letter grade for one hitter's recent form (total bases, hit%, RBI%, runs%, HR%, SB%, strikeout penalty). Default window is last 10 games.

families.name: report leaderboard
families.description: League-wide hitter report-card ranking when no player is given.

families.name: leaderboard audit
families.description: Replays the leaderboard's historical accuracy audit (predicted vs actual). No player needed.

families.name: combo bases
families.description: Combined total-bases analysis for a pair of players (teammates by default, or vs a common opponent), matched by shared game_id.

families.name: head-to-head (player vs/@ team)
families.description: A hitter's game log against one opponent team (regular-season source); @ scopes to away games only. -staff adds a per-pitcher career breakdown against that team's staff.
families.notes: -staff is only pre-computed for ~40 covered batters (data/output/mlb_bvp/*.json, see engines/mlb/bvp.py); other players simply get no staff section, no error. Spot-checked live -- works, prints a per-pitcher AB/H/HR/BB/K/AVG/OPS table.

families.name: postseason head-to-head
families.description: Same h2h shape as above, sourced from mlbpost_run instead of the regular-season scrape.
examples: nspe mlb post mookie betts vs PHI

families.name: home-run distance (long)
families.pattern: nspe mlb long -hrN -lastA/B | nspe mlb long -hr {min|max}N {-lastN|-season|-career|-YYYY|-YYYY-YYYY} | nspe mlb long -hrN -leaderboard {-lastN|-season|-career}
families.description: Home-run-distance-in-feet query family (from mlb_hr_tracker.json), mirroring NFL's 'long' explosive-play grammar: digit-attached -hrN is a per-event trend/leaderboard threshold, bare -hr + min/max is a compute total-distance threshold.

families.name: first plate-appearance outcome (first)
families.description: Categorical first-PA-of-the-game outcome tracker (from mlb_firstpa.json). No compute mode and no digit threshold -- an outcome either happened in a game or it didn't, so leaderboard (count) and trend (met A of B) are the only two shapes.
families.notes: `-hit` is a union of XBH-or-single (a walk doesn't count). Bare `nspe mlb first -xbh` with neither -leaderboard nor -lastA/B errors -- required, no default.

families.name: first-inning trend/leaderboard (inn1, legacy alt)
families.description: An earlier/parallel implementation of the same first-plate-appearance-outcome idea as 'mlb first' above, kept for backward compatibility. `inn1` is used (not `p1`) because `p1` is reserved for NHL period-1 scope.
families.notes: Functionally overlaps 'mlb first' -xbh/-walk/-hit but with slightly different outcome vocabulary (-extra instead of -xbh, plus -so for strikeout) -- both exist in the code side by side.

families.name: DraftKings hitter leaderboard
families.description: Hitters ranked by average real DraftKings fantasy points over a recent window (or an exact single-day slate via -yst). -leaderboard is required.

families.name: insight engine
families.description: Blends report-card form with team-allowed vulnerability to surface top prop suggestions for a given (or today's) slate.
families.notes: Not in any shell script; spot-checked live.

families.name: matchup crusher
families.description: Identifies batters who historically dominate today's opposing team; -season restricts the historical window to this season only (default career).
families.notes: Not in any shell script; spot-checked live.

families.name: parlay generator
families.description: Draws a randomized (score-weighted) parlay from a blended pool of hot-streak, matchup, batter-vs-pitcher, and first-PA signals; 'cut' instead prints the top ~15 shortlist itself for manual review, no parlay drawn.
families.notes: Repeated runs of the same non-'cut' format vary (weighted-random draw), by design -- not a fixed top-N.

families.name: goatcase (streak detector)
families.description: Detects and ranks players by consecutive-game streaks meeting a stat threshold in a given year; -goatcase alone means 3+ games, -goatcaseM sets a custom minimum streak length.
families.notes: Shared dispatch entry point also serves NBA and NFL (separate engines) -- see each league's own goatcase family. MLB stat vocabulary: hr, rbi, h, r, so, sb, 2b, 3b, tb.

families.name: compute
families.description: Sums passing/rushing/receiving yards or TDs across a window; with no window given, defaults to the current season (not career-wide). 'long' switches to explosive-play (PBP) counting instead of aggregated totals.
families.notes: -career and an explicit year filter are mutually exclusive (errors if both given).

families.name: compute modifiers: -td / -int / -tgts
families.pattern: nspe nfl <pass|rush|rec> -td {min|max}N ... | nspe nfl pass -int {min|max}N ... | nspe nfl rec -tgts {min|max}N ...
families.description: -td works for all three categories (switches summed field to touchdowns). -int is passing-only (interceptions) and errors on rush/rec. -tgts is receiving-only (targets) and errors on pass/rush.
families.notes: Verified live: `-int` on rush/rec and `-tgts` on pass/rush both produce a clear rejection error rather than a nonsensical field lookup. Bare `-tdN` (digit-attached) outside a trend query (-lastA/B) also errors, directing you to `-td minN` instead.

families.name: compute modifier: -splits
families.description: NFL's own -splits (separate implementation from the generic MLB/NBA/NHL one): breaks a career/multi-year total down by season, or a single-season total down by game.
families.notes: Not compatible with -long: `nspe nfl long pass -yds min50 -splits` errors explicitly ('-splits isn't supported with -long yet').

families.name: trend
families.description: QBs/RBs/WRs/TEs who hit a per-game yard or TD threshold in at least A of their last B games.
families.notes: nfl.sh uses an alternate '_td' suffix spelling for the TD trend variant (`pass_td -yds3 -last2/5`, `rush_td`, `rec_td`) -- functionally the same family as `<stat> -td<N>` seen elsewhere; both forms appear in the codebase's own test scripts.

families.name: leaderboard
families.description: Ranks players by total count of games (or explosive plays, for 'long') meeting a threshold.

families.name: streak
families.description: Consecutive-game streaks of a per-game threshold, regular season only (no postseason streak support for NFL).
examples: nspe nfl pass -yds250 -streak2 (see CFB equivalent; NFL streak follows the same shape per the format catalog)
families.notes: `-streakN` is not yet supported for NFL/CFB postseason data -- attempting it prints a clear error pointing to trend/compute/leaderboard alternatives instead.

families.name: combo
families.description: Combined-stat queries: -rr is rush+rec yards, -pr is pass+rush yards; verbose form -rush/-rec also works. -totalN is a context-dependent alias resolved by the nearest preceding pass/rush/rec keyword (pass always means pass+rush; rush/rec mean rush+rec).
examples: nspe cfb -rr100 -last3/5 (CFB shown; NFL shares the identical combo grammar per _NFL_FORMAT_CATALOG)

families.name: goatcase (streak detector)
families.description: Consecutive-game streak detector for pass/rush/rec yardage in a given year.
examples: nspe nfl -yds300 -goatcase 2025 (CFB equivalent; NFL's own goatcase.py mirrors it)
families.notes: NFL stat vocabulary for goatcase: yds, pass, rush, rec.

families.name: head-to-head (player vs/@ team)
families.description: A player's stat line against one specific opponent, with loose nickname/city/abbreviation team resolution.
examples: nspe nfl post dak vs PHI
families.notes: There is NO NFL equivalent of MLB's `-staff` flag (verified: no 'staff' reference anywhere in engines/nfl/h2h.py).

families.name: reference (win/loss record)
families.description: A player's team win/loss record (optionally filtered to wins/losses by at least N points margin), parsed from each game's result string.

families.name: week-N performance
families.description: A player's (QB-only) or team's average/aggregate performance in one specific regular-season week number, or a week range (-weekN-M). No window given defaults to the current season.
families.notes: QB mode is scoped to engines.nfl.qb_profile.STARTER_ROSTER only -- any other player gets a clear 'not supported yet' error, not a silently wrong answer. Team mode reuses the QB-pool game index, so its coverage for older seasons is bounded by how far back the team's CURRENT tracked QB's career reaches. Washington/Commanders has a known week-data gap for 2019-2021. Not present in any of the three shell scripts -- found via engine docstring, spot-checked live.

families.name: power rankings
families.description: Weighted composite team power ranking (efficiency + W/L + point margin, z-scored across all 32 teams), regular season only. Defaults to the 2025 season if no year given.
families.notes: Spot-checked live. Not present in the shell scripts -- built after they were written.

families.name: power rankings (team entry point)
families.description: Identical engine and output to 'nfl power' above, exposed as a second entry point under the 'team' namespace.
families.notes: Spot-checked live; output is byte-for-byte the same as `nspe nfl power` for the same year.

families.name: team head-to-head
families.description: Team-vs-team matchup history: box-score detail (yards/play, turnovers, time of possession) plus win/loss/score for every meeting in the window.
examples: nspe nfl team dal vs phi -career
families.notes: Spot-checked live. Unlike power rankings, this is NOT regular-season-only -- playoff meetings between the same two teams are included.

families.name: team points scored/allowed
families.pattern: nspe nfl team -ptsN|-allowedN -lastA/B | nspe nfl team -pts|-allowed {min|max}N {-lastN|-season|-YYYY|-YYYY-YYYY|-career} | nspe nfl team -pts|-allowed -leaderboard {-lastN|-season|-YYYY|-YYYY-YYYY|-career}
families.description: Trend/compute/leaderboard family for team-level points scored or allowed, derived from box scores already present in each player's row.
families.notes: `nspe nfl team -pts` with no min/max/-leaderboard/-lastA-B errors with a format catalog.

families.name: per-quarter passing/rushing/receiving
families.pattern: nspe nfl q1|q2|q3|q4|1h|h1 <pass|rush|rec> -ydsN -lastA/B | nspe nfl q1|q2|q3|q4|1h|h1 <pass|rush|rec> {min|max}N {-lastN|-season|-YYYY|-YYYY-YYYY|-career}
families.description: Trend/compute over yardage earned in one specific quarter or the first half only, from a dedicated PBP-derived data source (does not interact with 'long' or the regular gamelog).
families.notes: The pass|rush|rec category token is REQUIRED -- `nspe nfl q1 -yds50 -last1/3` (no category) errors explicitly with a format catalog. `h1` is an accepted alias for `1h`. Known data-quality caveat in the source: ~14% of rows don't sum-match the real box-score total (off by small amounts); ~0.5% of rows have a self-referential opponent bug and are dropped outright.

families.name: compute
families.description: Sums a stat across a window (or filters min/max total); supports a shorthand where digits attach directly to the stat token for a per-game (not total) filter context inside compute is unusual -- see 'trend' below for that shape.
families.notes: -total is an alias for -pts. -dub/-tripdub count double-doubles/triple-doubles rather than a raw stat total.

families.name: compute (multi-player selector)
families.description: Slash-separated player names run the same compute query for each named player instead of scanning the whole league.

families.name: trend
families.description: Players who hit a per-game threshold in at least A of their last B games.

families.name: leaderboard
families.description: Ranks players by count of qualifying games for a per-game threshold.
families.notes: -streakN cannot be combined with -leaderboard (separate engines; verified this errors).

families.name: streak
families.description: Every maximal run of N+ consecutive qualifying games, current season by default.

families.name: combo-stat
families.description: Per-game value = sum of two listed stats (pts/reb/ast/stl/blk/tpm). Routes to trend when -lastA/B is present, otherwise compute/streak. Shorthand `-stksN` = steals+blocks.
families.notes: Not supported under q1/1h quarter scope (no per-half ast/reb data yet).

families.name: q1 / 1h quarter-and-half scope
families.description: First-quarter or first-half-only points/three-pointers-made, sourced from a dedicated single-source-of-truth PBP dataset (playnba/<year>/1h/).

families.name: postseason
families.description: Same compute/trend/streak grammar as regular season, scoped to playoff gamelogs. Defaults to the current/most-recent postseason year unless a YYYY or YYYY-YYYY is given.

families.name: splits
families.description: Season-by-season or game-by-game breakdown instead of one collapsed total (shared generic compute-engine feature with MLB/NHL).
families.notes: Spot-checked live; not present in the shell scripts.

families.name: goatcase (streak detector)
families.description: Consecutive-game streak detector for an NBA stat in a given year.
examples: nspe nba -pts -goatcase 2024 (mirrors MLB/NFL goatcase shape; engines/nba/goatcase.py)
families.notes: Stat vocabulary: pts, reb, ast, stl, blk, fg, 3pt.

families.name: compute
families.description: Sums a stat (sog/g/ast/pts) across a window or filters by min/max total.

families.name: trend
families.description: Players who hit a per-game threshold in at least A of their last B games.

families.name: streak
families.description: Every maximal run of N+ consecutive qualifying games.

families.name: period scope (p1/p2/p3/ot)
families.pattern: nspe nhl p1|p2|p3|ot -<stat> {min|max}N | nspe nhl p1|p2|p3|ot <player>
families.description: Season-aggregate scoring-play points within one specific period (or OT). Every scorer AND assister on a scoring play earns 1 point in that play's period.
families.notes: Compute-only -- explicitly rejects -lastN/-season/-firstN windows with a clear error ('period data is season-aggregate only, try -pts minN'). No trend, streak, or leaderboard support for period scope.

families.name: postseason
families.description: Same compute/trend/streak grammar as regular season, scoped to playoff gamelogs.

families.name: splits
families.description: Season-by-season or game-by-game breakdown instead of one collapsed total (shared generic compute-engine feature with MLB/NBA).
families.notes: Not present in shell scripts; inferred/expected from the shared generic-compute -splits implementation (not individually spot-checked for NHL specifically, but the code path is identical to NBA/MLB).

limitations: NHL does NOT support a stat-token -leaderboard the way NBA does -- verified live: `nspe nhl -sog5 -leaderboard` errors with 'Unrecognized stat/option -leaderboard'. If you need an NHL leaderboard-style view, use -streakN or a compute min/max scan instead.

The NHL season had not yet started as of this catalog's generation date -- some current-season regular-season queries (e.g. -streak) may legitimately return empty results rather than indicating a bug.

families.name: compute
families.description: Sums passing/rushing/receiving yards or TDs across a window; mirrors NFL's compute grammar exactly, minus the explosive-play ('long') and -int/-tgts/-splits modifiers, which don't exist for CFB.
families.notes: -splits is silently accepted but has no effect for CFB (engines/cfb/stats.py's run_cfb_stats_query has no splits parameter at all) -- spot-checked live: `nspe cfb pass -yds min500 -splits -career` runs a normal career leaderboard, no error, no actual split-out breakdown. Worth fixing or documenting more loudly upstream.

families.description: QBs/RBs/receivers who hit a per-game yard/TD threshold in at least A of their last B games.

families.name: leaderboard

families.description: Consecutive-game streaks of a per-game threshold, regular season only (no postseason streak support).

families.name: combo (rush+rec)
families.description: Combined rush+receiving yards per game.

families.name: goatcase (streak detector) -- BROKEN
families.description: Documented in testnspe.sh as a working example (players with 3+ consecutive 300+ pass-yd game streaks), but the shared -goatcase dispatch in nspe_cli.py only has explicit routing branches for mlb/nba/nfl -- there is no engines/cfb/goatcase.py and no cfb branch in the dispatcher's if/elif chain.
families.notes: CONFIRMED BROKEN by direct execution: this exact command from testnspe.sh returns 'Error: Unknown league/stat combination for goatcase: cfb / YDS' instead of results. families.name: head-to-head (player vs/@ team)
families.description: A player's stat line against one specific ranked opponent (only AP top-25/tracked teams have data); supports nickname resolution.
families.notes: 'ncaaf' is a pure input alias for 'cfb' -- works identically everywhere. The tracked team roster is NOT a fixed 25/32 -- it grows dynamically from whatever team files exist in data/output/cfbscrape_results/ at runtime (starts at AP top-25, hard-capped at 32). Do not hardcode a team-count assumption when reasoning about CFB coverage.

families.name: reference (win/loss record)
families.description: A player's team win/loss record, optionally filtered by margin.
families.notes: Omitting 'ref' (e.g. `nspe cfb manning -wins -career`) is explicitly detected and errors with a hint to add 'ref', rather than silently misrouting.

meta_commands.name: plus (batch runner)
meta_commands.description: Runs up to 5 saved queries from data/plus_commands.json in one pass (each a pre-tokenized argv array, not a shell string) and writes a consolidated envelope to data/output/plus_results.json. Not a sport -- dispatched before any league parsing.

shared_tokens.meaning: Restrict to the player's most recent N games (compute: sum/filter over those N games; used as the window size for -lastA/B trend too).
Trend query: the stat threshold must be met in at least A of the player's last B games.
Same as -lastN/-lastA/B but anchored to the OLDEST N games in scope (season or year-window) instead of the most recent.
Scope to the current season only (all games), as opposed to a fixed -lastN window.
Sum/scan every available game with no season or window filter. Mutually exclusive with an explicit year filter for NFL compute.
Scope to one specific season year, or an inclusive range of years. The leading dash is optional in most parsers (both '-2024' and '2024' are accepted).

Exact-yesterday window: the player's real calendar-yesterday game specifically (not just their most-recent game, which could be older if they didn't play yesterday). Works for MLB compute/trend and MLB DK leaderboard.

Separate 'streak' engine (N>=2): reports every maximal run of N+ consecutive qualifying games. Cannot be combined with -leaderboard or -lastA/B trend tokens -- always used alone alongside the stat threshold.
Ranks players/teams by count of qualifying games (or, for MLB's bare `-leaderboard`, a weighted heat-score composite) instead of listing individual matches.
Limits a leaderboard's output to the top N rows.
Compute-mode threshold on a SUMMED total across the window (as opposed to a digit-attached stat token like -pts30, which is a PER-GAME threshold used by trend/leaderboard/streak).

Breaks a collapsed total down into its components: by season for a multi-season/career scope, by individual game for a single-season scope. Generic implementation shared by MLB/NBA/NHL; NFL has its own separate -splits implementation with the same idea.
Scopes to postseason data instead of the regular season. Accepted with or without a leading dash in most dispatch branches (both 'post' and '-post' work).
Head-to-head opponent selector. 'vs' means any game against that team; '@' restricts to away games only (MLB). Supports nickname/city/abbreviation resolution for the team name.
Quarter-or-half scope. NBA: first-quarter/first-half PBP for pts/tpm. NFL: per-quarter pass/rush/rec yardage (category token REQUIRED alongside the scope). 'h1' is accepted as an alias for '1h'.
NHL period scope (season-aggregate scoring-play points only; no -lastN/-season window support here -- compute-mode only).
MLB first-plate-appearance/first-inning scope (deliberately distinct from NHL's 'p1' to avoid a naming collision).
Consecutive-game streak detector across MLB/NBA/NFL (not CFB -- currently broken there, see cfb.goatcase family), given a year; M sets the minimum streak length (default 3).

MLB-specific: combined total-bases analysis for a pair of players (`<p1>/<p2> -combo`). Distinct from the NBA/NFL/CFB '-stat1/-stat2N' combo-stat token grammar, which sums two DIFFERENT stats for one player rather than combining two players.
MLB-only h2h modifier: adds a per-pitcher career breakdown against the opposing team's pitching staff (pre-computed for ~40 covered batters). No NFL equivalent exists.

NFL stat-family modifiers. -td: touchdowns instead of yards (pass/rush/rec all valid). -int: interceptions (passing only, errors elsewhere). -tgts: targets (receiving only, errors elsewhere). -long: switches source to play-by-play explosive-play data and prefixes the stat as 'long_<stat>'.
Combo-stat shorthand for NFL/CFB: -rr = rush+rec yards, -pr = pass+rush yards. Verbose equivalent: '-rush/-rec' / '-pass/-rush'.
Position filter, accepted as the token right after the league name for NFL and CFB (e.g. `nspe nfl qb pass ...`), or spelled out (quarterback/runningback/widereceiver/tightend).
Global flag (or NSPE_JSON=1 env var): suppresses/augments the human-readable table output with a single compact JSON envelope line on stdout, for programmatic consumers.
